strengths: Addresses an important problem with a practical approach: expanding training labels using existing graph nodes avoids synthesizing features and edges and applies across multiple GNN architectures.

The evaluation covers five datasets, three architectures, imbalance ratios up to 100, and five repetitions. Reported gains are substantial in several settings; for example, Cora-GCN at ratio 20 improves F1 from the strongest baseline's 66.82 to 74.15.

Pseudo-label accuracy analyses, component ablations, and sensitivity experiments provide useful evidence beyond aggregate performance. The appendix documents dataset distributions, optimization settings, hyperparameter ranges, and pseudocode.
weaknesses: Numerical inconsistencies undermine confidence in the supporting experiments. In Table 8, GCN at ratio 5 reports 11,593.60 aligned and 2,308.40 discarded nodes, totaling 13,902 despite only 13,632 unlabeled nodes. Table 9 reports 96.40 ± 4.27 as mean accuracy with standard error over five repetitions; the maximum possible conventional between-run standard error at that mean is 3.60 percentage points for accuracies bounded by 100%. Corrected tables and per-run results are needed.

Originality relative to M3S is insufficiently established. Section 6 acknowledges that M3S already filters pseudo-labels through clustering/prediction agreement, closely resembling DPAM. Although the DPAM-plus-confidence ablations are informative, an explicit comparison with M3S under identical class quotas and retraining settings is missing. The contribution beyond this closely related method remains uncertain.

The geometric filter has a consequential definition mismatch. Equation 5 measures distance to the assigned class center, while Section 4.3 assumes this is the nearest class center. Assigning labels through cluster centroids and classifier agreement does not guarantee that property for individual nodes. Consequently, the stated ordering of distances and interpretation of the GI index need correction. Equation 7 also needs an explicit definition of how sorted lists become per-node numerical ranks.

The ablations provide mixed support for the proposed refinements. In Table 11, geometric ranking alone nearly matches the full method on Cora-GCN (75.85 versus 76.44) and PubMed-GAT (77.32 versus 77.38); removing DGIN improves CiteSeer-SAGE (58.71 versus 57.51). A fixed-weight rank-fusion comparison is needed to establish the benefit of RBO-based weighting. Claims that every component improves performance are too strong.

Some broader experimental claims exceed the evidence. UNREAL trails GraphENS+TAM on Computers-Random with GraphSAGE in both metrics, contradicting the claimed consistent superiority on naturally imbalanced datasets. Furthermore, changing the majority-label budget and training split between imbalance settings confounds conclusions about the isolated effect of increasing imbalance.

Reproducibility and computational tradeoffs remain incompletely documented. The manuscript does not specify the F1 averaging convention, selected configurations, or whether retraining restarts model parameters. With 40-100 selection rounds, repeated clustering, and up to 2,000 training epochs per later round, runtime and peak-memory measurements are necessary to substantiate computational advantages; baseline out-of-memory results alone are insufficient.
